intent.raw_query: Morocco Marrakech and Sahara, $1000 solo, 7 days, March

experiences.name: Djemaa el-Fna Square & Medina Exploration
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in the beating heart of Marrakech by wandering the UNESCO-listed Djemaa el-Fna square. Watch snake charmers, storytellers, and musicians by day, then stay for the magical transformation at dusk when food stalls fill the air with smoke and spices. Explore the labyrinthine souks of the surrounding medina, bargaining for spices, leather goods, and handwoven textiles.

experiences.name: Sahara Desert Camel Trek & Overnight Camp
experiences.description: Journey to the golden dunes of Erg Chebbi near Merzouga and embark on a sunset camel trek into the Sahara. Spend the night in a traditional Berber camp under a breathtaking canopy of stars, enjoy live Gnawa music around a campfire, sip mint tea, and wake before dawn to witness a spectacular desert sunrise over the dunes.

experiences.name: Traditional Moroccan Cooking Class
experiences.description: Join a local chef in a riad kitchen for a hands-on cooking class where you learn to prepare authentic Moroccan dishes such as lamb tagine with preserved lemon, harira soup, and honey-drenched pastilla. Begin with a guided tour of the spice souks to source fresh ingredients like ras el hanout, saffron, and argan oil before cooking and dining together.

experiences.name: Bahia Palace & Saadian Tombs Historical Tour
experiences.description: Step back into the grandeur of Moroccan imperial history with a self-guided or locally led tour of the 19th-century Bahia Palace, adorned with intricate zellige tilework, carved cedarwood ceilings, and lush courtyards. Continue to the nearby Saadian Tombs, a hidden necropolis of the 16th-century Saadian dynasty rediscovered in 1917, featuring stunning marble and stucco craftsmanship.

experiences.name: Ksar of Aït Benhaddou & Draa Valley Drive
experiences.description: Travel through the dramatic Atlas Mountain passes to the UNESCO World Heritage ksar (fortified village) of Aït Benhaddou, a stunning example of southern Moroccan earthen clay architecture and a famous film location for Gladiator and Game of Thrones. Continue into the lush Draa Valley, dotted with ancient kasbahs, date palm oases, and Berber villages, stopping for a traditional lunch of mechoui (slow-roasted lamb) at a local auberge.
experiences.location: Aït Benhaddou & Draa Valley, Ouarzazate Province

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Marrakech Menara Airport at 22:30. Take a petit taxi (negotiate fare, ~80-100 MAD) to Hotel Aday in Derb Sidi Bouloukat, located in the heart of the Medina. Check in, freshen up, and get a good night's rest. If hungry, grab a quick snack from a nearby street stall still open late near Jemaa el-Fna square (5-10 min walk).

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or airport
meals.dinner: Late-night street food near Jemaa el-Fna – try a msemen (flatbread) with honey or a bowl of harira soup for 10-20 MAD

day_by_day.notes: Keep some Moroccan Dirhams (MAD) ready before leaving the airport – exchange at the airport bureau or use an ATM. Confirm hotel check-in for late arrival in advance. Petit taxis are metered but drivers often negotiate at night; agree on price before getting in.

day_by_day.morning: After a hearty riad breakfast, head out to explore the iconic Jemaa el-Fna square (5-min walk from hotel). Soak in the morning atmosphere with orange juice vendors (4 MAD/glass) and snake charmers. Then dive into the souks – explore Souk Semmarine (textiles), Souk des Épices (spice market), and Souk Chouari (woodworkers). Bargaining is expected; browse freely without obligation to buy.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Bahia Palace (entrance ~70 MAD) – a stunning 19th-century palace with intricate Moroccan tilework, carved cedar ceilings, and lush gardens. Afterward, walk to the nearby Mellah (Jewish Quarter) and explore the historic Lazama Synagogue (free or small donation). Stroll through the covered market streets of the Mellah for a quieter, authentic experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Jemaa el-Fna as it transforms into a massive open-air food market. Grab a numbered stall dinner – try grilled kefta, merguez sausages, snail soup (babbouche), or couscous. Watch street performers, storytellers, and musicians for free. End the night with a mint tea at a rooftop café overlooking the square.

meals.breakfast: Included at Hotel Aday or nearby café – msemen, amlou (almond-argan dip), mint tea (~20-30 MAD if not included)
meals.lunch: Cheap local restaurant near the souks – try a set menu (menu du jour) with soup, tagine, and bread for 40-60 MAD
meals.dinner: Jemaa el-Fna food stalls – full meal with grilled meats, salads, and bread for 50-80 MAD

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes – the Medina streets are cobblestone and uneven. Keep your bag close in crowded souk areas. Bargain for everything in the souks; start at 30-40% of the asking price. The Bahia Palace is best visited in the morning or afternoon to avoid tour groups.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Saadian Tombs (entrance ~70 MAD) – a beautifully preserved 16th-century royal necropolis hidden for centuries. Arrive early to beat crowds. Then walk to the Kasbah Mosque area and explore the surrounding Kasbah neighborhood, one of Marrakech's oldest districts. Stop at a local bakery (farran) to watch traditional bread being baked in a communal wood-fired oven.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Mellah's El Badi Palace ruins (entrance ~70 MAD) – a once-magnificent 16th-century palace now in atmospheric ruins, offering great views from the ramparts. Afterward, visit the Museum of Moroccan Arts (Dar Si Said) nearby (~30 MAD) to see traditional Berber jewelry, carpets, and woodwork. Walk back through the southern Medina streets, stopping at artisan workshops.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Mouassine neighborhood – one of Marrakech's most authentic quarters. Visit the Mouassine Fountain and the grand Mouassine Mosque (exterior only). Have dinner at a local neighborhood restaurant away from the tourist center for better prices and authenticity. End with a walk through the quieter evening souks.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or street-side café – coffee, msemen, and olive oil for 15-25 MAD
meals.lunch: Snack lunch near El Badi Palace – sandwich with kefta or merguez from a street cart (15-25 MAD) plus fresh-squeezed orange juice (4 MAD)
meals.dinner: Local restaurant in Mouassine quarter – chicken or lamb tagine with bread and salad for 50-70 MAD

day_by_day.notes: The Saadian Tombs and El Badi Palace are close to each other – plan them on the same day to save walking time. Combo tickets may be available. Photography is allowed at El Badi Palace ruins. Dress modestly when near mosques (shoulders and knees covered).

day_by_day.morning: Early departure (6:00-7:00 AM) for the Sahara Desert via a shared budget group tour or rented grand taxi to Ouarzazate and Merzouga. Book a budget shared minibus tour (1,200-1,800 MAD for 2-day/1-night Sahara tour including transport, accommodation, and camel ride) through your hotel or a Medina agency the day before. The scenic drive crosses the High Atlas Mountains via the Tizi n'Tichka pass (2,260m) – stunning mountain and valley views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at Aït Benhaddou (UNESCO World Heritage ksar/fortified village) en route – a breathtaking ancient earthen city used in films like Gladiator and Game of Thrones. Explore the ksar on foot (small entrance fee ~10-20 MAD). Continue driving through the Draa Valley with its palm groves and kasbahs toward the Sahara. Arrive in the Merzouga/Erg Chebbi dune area by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Mount camels at sunset for a 1-hour ride into the Erg Chebbi dunes (included in tour). Watch the spectacular Sahara sunset from the top of the golden dunes. Spend the night at a budget desert camp (included in tour) – traditional Berber tents with basic bedding. Enjoy a campfire dinner with Berber music and drumming under an extraordinary star-filled sky.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at hotel before departure – bread, jam, coffee (included or 20-30 MAD)
meals.lunch: Roadside restaurant stop en route – Moroccan set menu with tagine and salad (50-70 MAD, sometimes included in tour)
meals.dinner: Included at desert camp – traditional Berber meal with tagine, couscous, salads, and mint tea around the campfire

day_by_day.notes: Book the Sahara tour 1-2 days in advance from your hotel or a reputable Medina agency. Compare prices from 2-3 agencies. Shared group tours are the most budget-friendly option. Pack a light jacket – desert nights in March can be cold (5-10°C). Bring sunscreen, sunglasses, a scarf (for sand), and a headlamp. Charge all devices before leaving Marrakech.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before sunrise (5:30 AM) to climb the dunes and watch the magical Sahara sunrise – one of the most memorable experiences of the trip. Take photos, enjoy the silence, and have a simple breakfast at camp. Begin the return journey to Marrakech via a different scenic route through the Todra Gorge (dramatic 300m-high limestone canyon) or the Dades Valley (Valley of a Thousand Kasbahs) depending on tour itinerary.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the scenic drive back through the Atlas Mountains. Stop at a roadside argan oil cooperative to see how argan oil is traditionally produced by Berber women (free to visit, no obligation to buy). Arrive back in Marrakech by late afternoon (around 17:00-19:00). Check back into Hotel Aday, shower, and rest.
day_by_day.evening: Gentle evening stroll through the Medina to decompress after the long journey. Visit the Cyber Park (Arset el Harti) – a free public garden near the Medina walls, popular with locals in the evening. Have a relaxed dinner at a local restaurant. Early night to recover from the desert adventure.

meals.breakfast: Simple breakfast at desert camp – bread, jam, Moroccan pancakes, mint tea (included in tour)
meals.lunch: Roadside stop en route – tagine or sandwich at a local restaurant (40-60 MAD)
meals.dinner: Local Medina restaurant near hotel – vegetable or chicken tagine with khobz bread (45-65 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: The return drive is long (8-10 hours with stops). Bring snacks and water for the journey. The Todra Gorge stop is highly recommended if your tour includes it. Rest well tonight as Day 6 involves more Marrakech exploration.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Majorelle Garden (entrance 150 MAD – worth the splurge) – a stunning cobalt-blue botanical garden created by French painter Jacques Majorelle and later owned by Yves Saint Laurent. Also visit the small Berber Museum within the garden (included in ticket). Arrive at opening time (8:00 AM) to avoid crowds. Afterward, explore the Gueliz neighborhood (New City) – a contrast to the Medina with French colonial architecture and modern cafés.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the Medina for a deeper souk experience. Visit the Dyers' Quarter (Souk des Teinturiers) to see wool being dyed in vivid colors. Explore the Fondouks (ancient merchant caravanserais) – Fondouk el-Amira Mina is one of the most photogenic. Stop at the Ben Youssef Madrasa (entrance ~70 MAD) – a stunning 14th-century Islamic college with intricate zellij tilework, carved stucco, and cedar woodwork. One of Morocco's most beautiful historic buildings.
day_by_day.evening: Splurge slightly on a traditional hammam experience – try a local neighborhood hammam (not a tourist spa) for 15-30 MAD for the basic scrub and steam. Ask your hotel to recommend a nearby authentic one. Afterward, enjoy a final proper Marrakech dinner at a mid-range local restaurant. Stroll Jemaa el-Fna one last time to soak in the atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Café in Gueliz – café au lait and croissant or msemen (20-35 MAD)
meals.lunch: Cheap eats in the Medina – bissara (fava bean soup) with bread and olive oil, a classic Moroccan budget meal (15-25 MAD)
meals.dinner: Slightly nicer local restaurant for a farewell Marrakech meal – pastilla (sweet-savory pigeon pie) or mechoui (slow-roasted lamb) for 80-120 MAD

day_by_day.notes: Majorelle Garden is the priciest single attraction but genuinely spectacular – budget for it. Arrive at opening time to get photos without crowds. The Ben Youssef Madrasa is a must-see for history and architecture lovers. For the hammam, bring flip-flops and a change of underwear; towels are usually provided.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech – visit the lively Sunday Mellah Market for fresh produce, olives, preserved lemons, spices, and local goods at very low prices. Great for picking up authentic food souvenirs (argan oil, ras el hanout spice mix, dried rose petals). Do any last-minute souvenir shopping in the souks – leather goods, Berber rugs, lanterns, and ceramics are popular buys. Bargain hard for the best prices.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time, enjoy a final mint tea at a rooftop café overlooking the Medina rooftops. Visit the Koutoubia Mosque gardens (exterior and gardens are free) – the 12th-century minaret is Marrakech's most iconic landmark and the model for the Giralda in Seville. Take a final walk along the Medina ramparts. Head back to hotel to collect luggage and arrange transport to the airport (petit taxi ~80-100 MAD or negotiate a grand taxi).
day_by_day.evening: Depart Marrakech with incredible memories of the Medina, Sahara dunes, mountain passes, and Berber culture. If flight is late evening, enjoy one last harira soup or mint tea near the airport area.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast or street-side café – msemen with honey and argan oil, mint tea (20-30 MAD)
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the Koutoubia – sandwich, fresh juice, and pastries from a local bakery (25-40 MAD)
meals.dinner: Airport or pre-departure snack – grab some Moroccan cookies (ghriba) or dates for the journey home

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5-3 hours before your flight for airport check-in and security. The airport is about 20-30 minutes from the Medina by taxi. Pack any liquid food souvenirs (argan oil, olive oil) in checked luggage. Declare any large cash amounts if required. Total estimated budget for 7 days (excluding flights): 2,500-3,500 MAD (~$250-350 USD) per person, including accommodation, food, transport, tours, and entrance fees.

trip_options.title: Classic Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival at 22:30. Check in to Hotel Aday, freshen up, and rest.
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — in transit.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Marrakech Menara Airport at 22:30. Take a pre-arranged airport transfer or petit taxi (~80–100 MAD) to Hotel Aday in Derb Sidi Bouloukat, Medina. Check in, settle into your riad-style surroundings, and get a good night's sleep.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport.
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport.
meals.dinner: If hungry upon arrival, grab a light snack from a 24-hour convenience store near the Medina or ask the hotel for a late-night option. Many riads can arrange a simple welcome mint tea and pastries.

day_by_day.notes: Flight UA arrives at 22:30. Allow 45–60 minutes for immigration, baggage claim, and transfer. Hotel Aday is located inside the Medina — confirm exact drop-off point with the hotel in advance as cars cannot always enter narrow derbs. Keep some Moroccan Dirhams (MAD) handy for the taxi.

day_by_day.morning: Start with a traditional Moroccan breakfast at the hotel or a nearby café. Then explore the iconic Djemaa el-Fna square (5-minute walk), soaking in the morning atmosphere with orange juice vendors and street performers. Visit the nearby Koutoubia Mosque gardens for a peaceful stroll and great photos of the minaret.
day_by_day.afternoon: Dive into the historic Medina souks — explore the spice market (Rahba Kedima), leather tanneries (Chouara viewpoint from a nearby shop terrace), and the dyers' souk. Hire a local guide from the square (~150–200 MAD for 2 hours) for authentic context. Visit the Ben Youssef Madrasa, one of Morocco's most stunning Islamic schools (entry ~70 MAD).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Djemaa el-Fna at sunset to witness its magical transformation — snake charmers, storytellers, musicians, and dozens of food stalls light up the square. Enjoy the lively atmosphere before dinner.

meals.breakfast: At Hotel Aday or Café des Épices near the Rahba Kedima — try msemen (Moroccan flatbread), amlou (almond-argan dip), and mint tea (~30–50 MAD).
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local Medina restaurant such as Le Jardin or a hole-in-the-wall near the souks — try harira soup, kefta sandwich, or a tagine (~60–100 MAD).
meals.dinner: Eat at the Djemaa el-Fna food stalls — try merguez sausages, grilled lamb, snail soup, and fresh-squeezed orange juice (~80–120 MAD). Alternatively, dine at Restaurant Chez Bahia for a sit-down Moroccan meal.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — the Medina streets are cobblestone and uneven. Bargaining is expected in the souks; start at 40–50% of the asking price. Keep your belongings secure in crowded areas. March weather in Marrakech is pleasant (~18–24°C), ideal for walking.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Saadian Tombs (entry ~70 MAD), a beautifully preserved 16th-century royal necropolis just a short walk from the hotel. Then head to the El Badi Palace ruins (~70 MAD) — a vast 16th-century palace complex with panoramic rooftop views and resident storks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Mellah (Jewish Quarter) and its historic synagogues. Visit the Bahia Palace (~70 MAD), a stunning 19th-century palace with intricate Moroccan craftsmanship, painted ceilings, and lush gardens. Spend time wandering the quieter southern Medina streets.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Mouassine neighborhood for a relaxed evening. Browse the upscale boutiques and concept stores around Mouassine Fountain. Enjoy a rooftop sunset drink (fresh juice or Moroccan lemonade) at a café overlooking the Medina rooftops.

meals.breakfast: At the hotel — enjoy a full Moroccan spread with khobz bread, olive oil, honey, and mint tea.
meals.lunch: Try Nomad Restaurant near Rahba Kedima for modern Moroccan cuisine with a rooftop view (~120–180 MAD per person).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Dar Zitoun or a similar mid-range Moroccan restaurant in the Mellah area — try pastilla (pigeon pie), lamb tagine with prunes, and bastilla au lait for dessert (~150–200 MAD).

day_by_day.notes: The Saadian Tombs can get crowded mid-morning — arrive early. The Bahia Palace is best visited in the afternoon when tour groups thin out. Keep a small notebook or use Google Maps offline as the Medina lanes can be confusing.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early (~7:00 AM) on a shared or private 3-day Sahara desert tour departing from Marrakech. The route crosses the stunning High Atlas Mountains via the Tizi n'Tichka pass (2,260m). Stop at Aït Benhaddou — a UNESCO World Heritage ksar (fortified village) used in films like Gladiator and Game of Thrones. Explore the ancient mud-brick citadel on foot (~1.5 hours).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through the Draa Valley, passing kasbahs, palm groves, and dramatic desert landscapes. Arrive in Ouarzazate — the 'Hollywood of Morocco.' Optional stop at Atlas Film Studios (entry ~50 MAD) to see famous movie sets. Continue driving toward Boumalne Dades and the Dades Gorge.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at a mid-range guesthouse or kasbah hotel in the Dades Valley. Enjoy the dramatic gorge scenery at dusk. Relax and prepare for the next day's desert journey.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departure — pack snacks for the road.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local restaurant in Aït Benhaddou village — try a Berber tagine or couscous (~80–120 MAD).
meals.dinner: Dinner at your Dades Valley guesthouse — traditional Moroccan dinner included in most mid-range desert tour packages (~150–200 MAD if not included).

day_by_day.notes: Book a reputable 3-day Sahara tour in advance (~1,500–2,500 MAD per person for shared tours including transport, accommodation, and camel ride). Departure is early — pack the night before. Bring layers as the Atlas Mountains can be cold in March. The drive from Marrakech to Dades is approximately 5–6 hours with stops.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early to explore the Dades Gorge — the dramatic rock formations known as 'Monkey Fingers' are best seen in morning light. Short hike or drive through the gorge. Continue the journey east through the Todra Gorge — towering 300m limestone canyon walls, one of Morocco's most spectacular natural sites. Walk through the narrow gorge floor.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive through the Ziz Valley and Erfoud, gateway to the Sahara. Stop at fossil shops in Erfoud (the region is famous for trilobite fossils). Continue to Merzouga, the village at the edge of the Erg Chebbi dunes — the iconic orange sand dunes of the Moroccan Sahara rising up to 150m.
day_by_day.evening: Mount camels at sunset for a 1-hour camel trek into the Erg Chebbi dunes. Arrive at a mid-range desert camp — enjoy a Berber dinner under the stars, traditional music around the campfire, and an extraordinary stargazing experience in one of Africa's darkest skies.

meals.breakfast: At the Dades guesthouse — Moroccan breakfast with bread, olive oil, and mint tea.
meals.lunch: Quick lunch in Erfoud or a roadside stop — try a Berber omelette or sandwich (~60–80 MAD).
meals.dinner: Traditional Berber dinner at the desert camp — tagine, couscous, Moroccan salads, and mint tea around the campfire (usually included in tour package).

day_by_day.notes: Bring a headscarf or turban for the camel ride — sand can be blowing. Temperatures in the Sahara in March are ideal (~25°C days, ~8–12°C nights) — bring a warm layer for the evening. Charge all devices before leaving for the camp as electricity may be limited. The camel ride is approximately 1 hour each way.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before sunrise (~5:30 AM) to climb a dune and watch the Sahara sunrise — one of the most breathtaking experiences of the trip. Take photos, meditate, or simply absorb the silence of the desert. Return to camp for breakfast. Optional: sandboarding on the dunes or a 4x4 excursion around the erg (~100–150 MAD extra).
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the return journey to Marrakech via a different route — through the Ziz Gorge, Midelt, and the Middle Atlas Mountains. The landscape shifts dramatically from desert to cedar forests. Stop in Midelt for lunch. Continue through Azrou (possible Barbary macaque sighting in the cedar forest) and Ifrane — Morocco's 'Little Switzerland.'
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Marrakech (~21:00–22:00). Check back into Hotel Aday. Unwind with a mint tea and reflect on the desert adventure.

meals.breakfast: At the desert camp — simple Berber breakfast with bread, honey, and argan oil.
meals.lunch: Lunch in Midelt — try a hearty Berber tagine or lamb chops at a local restaurant (~80–120 MAD).
meals.dinner: Late dinner near the hotel upon return — grab a quick bite at a Medina restaurant or order from the hotel if available (~80–120 MAD).

day_by_day.notes: The return drive is approximately 8–9 hours with stops — it's a long day. Bring water, snacks, and entertainment. The Middle Atlas route is scenic but can be cold in March — keep a jacket accessible. Confirm return drop-off point with your tour operator (ideally at your hotel or Djemaa el-Fna).

day_by_day.morning: Spend a leisurely final morning in Marrakech. Visit the Majorelle Garden (entry ~150 MAD) — a stunning botanical garden with cobalt-blue villa, designed by French painter Jacques Majorelle and later restored by Yves Saint Laurent. Also visit the adjacent Berber Museum. Stroll through the Guéliz (New City) neighborhood for a contrast to the Medina.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the Medina for last-minute souvenir shopping — argan oil, Moroccan leather goods, spices, lanterns, and ceramics. Visit the Ensemble Artisanal (fixed-price government cooperative) for fair-priced authentic crafts without bargaining pressure. Treat yourself to a traditional hammam experience (~150–250 MAD) at a local hammam near the hotel for a relaxing send-off.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a final Moroccan dinner at a special restaurant. Pack, settle the hotel bill, and arrange airport transfer for your departure (if flying out tonight or early next morning).

meals.breakfast: Final Moroccan breakfast at the hotel or at Grand Café de la Poste in Guéliz — enjoy a leisurely meal with café au lait and croissants (~60–100 MAD).
meals.lunch: Lunch at Café Arabe in the Mouassine neighborhood — beautiful courtyard setting, Moroccan-Mediterranean menu (~150–200 MAD).
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly on a farewell dinner at Le Tobsil or Dar Yacout — a traditional Moroccan feast in a stunning riad setting with live music (~350–500 MAD per person, book in advance).

day_by_day.notes: Majorelle Garden is very popular — arrive at opening time (9:00 AM) to avoid crowds. The hammam is a must-do cultural experience — ask the hotel to recommend a reputable local hammam. Keep some MAD for tips, last-minute purchases, and taxi to the airport. Marrakech Menara Airport is approximately 15–20 minutes from the Medina by taxi (~80–100 MAD).

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight UA arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Marrakech Menara Airport at 22:30. Private luxury transfer arranged to Hotel Aday in the heart of the Medina (Derb Sidi Bouloukat). Check in, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome mint tea and light snack prepared by the riad staff. Settle into your suite and rest after the journey.

meals.breakfast: On board or at airport
meals.lunch: On board or at airport
meals.dinner: Late-night welcome platter of Moroccan mezze and pastilla bites arranged by the riad — dates, olives, harissa, and warm khobz bread served in your room or private courtyard

day_by_day.notes: Confirm private airport transfer in advance. Hotel Aday is a boutique riad — the narrow Medina lanes require a local guide or tuk-tuk for the final approach from the drop-off point. Keep luggage manageable for the last 100m walk through the derb (alley).

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely start with a traditional Moroccan breakfast on the riad rooftop terrace. At 10:00, begin a private guided walking tour of the Medina — explore the iconic Djemaa el-Fna square in the morning calm before the crowds arrive, then wind through the historic souks: spice market (Rahba Kedima), leather tanneries viewpoint, and the dyers' souk. Visit the 14th-century Ben Youssef Madrasa, one of the most stunning examples of Moorish architecture in North Africa.
day_by_day.afternoon: After lunch, visit the Bahia Palace (Palais de la Bahia) — a 19th-century masterpiece of Moroccan craftsmanship with ornate tilework, carved cedar ceilings, and lush gardens. Continue to the Saadian Tombs, a royal necropolis dating to the 16th century, rediscovered only in 1917. End the afternoon with a private calligraphy or zellige tile-making workshop arranged through the hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll back through Djemaa el-Fna at dusk as the square transforms — snake charmers, storytellers, and food stalls ignite the night. Enjoy pre-dinner cocktails (or fresh-pressed juices) at a rooftop terrace bar overlooking the square. Dinner at a premium restaurant in the Medina.

meals.breakfast: Riad rooftop breakfast — msemen (flaky flatbread), amlou (argan oil & almond dip), fresh-squeezed orange juice, Moroccan mint tea, honey, and seasonal fruit
meals.lunch: Lunch at Nomad Restaurant (Derb Aarjan, Medina) — contemporary Moroccan cuisine with rooftop views; try the lamb pastilla and harira soup
meals.dinner: Dinner at Le Foundouk (55 Souk Hal Fassi) — a beautifully restored 18th-century caravanserai serving refined Moroccan-French cuisine; reserve the mezzanine for the best ambiance

day_by_day.notes: Book Ben Youssef Madrasa tickets in advance — timed entry recommended. Private guide for the morning souk walk enhances the experience significantly and helps avoid tourist traps. Dress modestly for religious and historical sites.

day_by_day.morning: Morning visit to the Majorelle Garden — the iconic cobalt-blue botanical garden once owned by Yves Saint Laurent, now home to the Berber Museum (Musée Berbère). Arrive at opening (09:00) to enjoy it before the midday crowds. Explore the YSL Memorial and the adjacent MIAM (Musée Yves Saint Laurent Marrakech) for a fascinating intersection of fashion, art, and Moroccan culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private cooking class at a premium culinary atelier in the Medina (such as La Maison Arabe Cooking School or Souk Cuisine). Learn to prepare a traditional Moroccan feast: harira soup, chicken tagine with preserved lemon and olives, couscous with seven vegetables, and bastilla au lait for dessert. This is a hands-on, immersive 3-hour experience with a local chef.
day_by_day.evening: Hammam and spa experience at a luxury hammam (such as Les Bains de Marrakech or Royal Mansour Spa if accessible). Enjoy a traditional black soap scrub (kessa), ghassoul clay mask, and argan oil massage. Return to the riad refreshed for a relaxed dinner.

meals.breakfast: Riad breakfast — beghrir (semolina pancakes with honey butter), soft-boiled eggs, fresh fruit platter, and Moroccan coffee
meals.lunch: Enjoy the dishes you prepared during the cooking class — a convivial lunch with your instructor and fellow guests in a traditional Moroccan dining room
meals.dinner: Dinner at Dar Yacout (79 Sidi Ahmed Soussi) — a legendary Marrakech institution set in a stunning riad; multi-course Moroccan feast with live Gnawa music; advance reservation essential

day_by_day.notes: Majorelle Garden tickets sell out — book online at least 48 hours ahead. The YSL Museum requires a separate ticket. Hammam sessions should be booked 24 hours in advance. Dar Yacout is one of Marrakech's most celebrated dining experiences — dress elegantly.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Marrakech at 07:00 by private luxury 4x4 vehicle for the journey to the Sahara Desert (Merzouga/Erg Chebbi). The route crosses the dramatic High Atlas Mountains via the Tizi n'Tichka pass (2,260m) — stop for photos at the summit and visit the UNESCO-listed Aït Benhaddou ksar (fortified village), a breathtaking 11th-century earthen citadel that has served as a backdrop for films including Gladiator and Game of Thrones. Private guided tour of the ksar included.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through the Draa Valley and the Valley of Roses (Vallée des Roses) — a stunning gorge lined with rose bushes, kasbahs, and palm groves. Stop at a local cooperative to learn about rose water and argan oil production. Pass through Ouarzazate (the 'Hollywood of Africa') and continue toward the desert. Arrive at your luxury desert camp or kasbah hotel near Merzouga by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Mount your camel at sunset for a guided ride into the golden dunes of Erg Chebbi — the most spectacular sand sea in Morocco, with dunes reaching 150m. Watch the sunset from the top of a dune with a glass of Moroccan tea. Overnight at a premium luxury desert camp (private ensuite tent with real beds, electricity, and hot showers).

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the riad before departure — packed travel breakfast if needed
meals.lunch: Lunch at a scenic restaurant in Aït Benhaddou village — traditional Berber tagine and fresh salads with Atlas Mountain views
meals.dinner: Dinner under the stars at the luxury desert camp — traditional Moroccan feast around a fire pit with live Berber music (guembri and bendir drums); menu includes mechoui (slow-roasted lamb), couscous, and Saharan mint tea ceremony

day_by_day.notes: The Marrakech–Merzouga drive is approximately 8–9 hours with stops — an early departure is essential. Alternatively, a scenic flight to Ouarzazate can shorten the journey (check availability). Pack a light jacket — desert nights in March can drop to 5–10°C. Bring sunscreen, sunglasses, and a scarf for the dunes.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before dawn (05:30) for a private sunrise hike to the top of the highest dune in Erg Chebbi — an unforgettable experience as the Sahara turns from deep purple to blazing gold. Return to camp for a leisurely Berber breakfast. Optional: sandboarding on the dunes or a 4x4 desert excursion to visit a nomadic Berber family in their traditional tent — share tea and learn about their way of life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the desert camp and visit the Merzouga village and the shores of Dayet Srji — a seasonal salt lake that attracts flamingos in spring (March is an excellent time). Visit a local fossil and mineral workshop — the Sahara region is world-famous for its trilobite and ammonite fossils. Begin the return journey westward, stopping at the Todra Gorge — a spectacular canyon with 300m-high rose-colored limestone walls, perfect for a scenic walk along the river.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at a luxury kasbah hotel in the Draa Valley or Skoura oasis for the night (such as Kasbah Bab Ourika or Dar Ahlam if routing allows). Enjoy a private terrace dinner overlooking a palm grove.

meals.breakfast: Berber breakfast at the desert camp — khobz, olive oil, honey, argan amlou, hard-boiled eggs, fresh mint tea, and dates
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch prepared by the camp — Moroccan sandwiches, fresh fruit, and juice enjoyed at the Todra Gorge riverside
meals.dinner: Dinner at your kasbah hotel — refined Moroccan cuisine featuring local specialties such as lamb with prunes and almonds, served in a candlelit courtyard

day_by_day.notes: The sunrise dune climb is the highlight of the Sahara experience — do not miss it. Wear closed shoes for the dune walk. The Todra Gorge is most dramatic in the late afternoon light. Confirm your kasbah hotel booking well in advance as luxury properties in the valley have limited rooms.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure at the kasbah — optional yoga session on the rooftop or a guided walk through the palmery (palm grove oasis). Depart after breakfast and continue the return journey to Marrakech via the scenic Ourika Valley route or the Tizi n'Tichka pass. Stop at a traditional Berber argan oil cooperative run by women — learn about the labor-intensive process of hand-cracking argan nuts and purchase authentic cold-pressed argan oil directly from the source.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive back in Marrakech by early afternoon. Check back into Hotel Aday. Spend the afternoon on a curated luxury shopping experience in the Medina souks with a private guide — focus on high-quality artisan goods: hand-knotted Berber rugs, silver jewelry, hand-painted ceramics, bespoke leather babouches (slippers), and pure argan oil products. Visit a reputable fixed-price artisan cooperative to avoid bargaining stress.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a rooftop bar with panoramic Medina views (Sky Bar at the Selman Hotel or Kabana Rooftop). Final evening in Marrakech — a special farewell dinner at one of the city's most prestigious restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Full Moroccan breakfast at the kasbah — a lavish spread of local cheeses, honey, msemen, fresh-squeezed juices, and mint tea
meals.lunch: Light lunch en route — stop at a roadside café in the Atlas foothills for a simple but authentic harira soup and Moroccan salads
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at La Mamounia's Le Marocain restaurant — the most iconic luxury dining experience in Marrakech, set in the legendary La Mamounia palace hotel; traditional Moroccan cuisine elevated to haute cuisine; full evening dress recommended

day_by_day.notes: La Mamounia's Le Marocain requires advance reservation and smart dress code. The return drive from the desert is approximately 5–6 hours — plan accordingly. The argan cooperative visit is best arranged through your hotel or guide to ensure authenticity.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech — enjoy a slow breakfast on the riad rooftop. Take a peaceful early morning walk through the Medina before the souks open — the narrow alleys are magical in the quiet morning light. Visit the Koutoubia Mosque gardens (the mosque exterior and gardens are open to non-Muslims) — the 12th-century minaret is the architectural inspiration for the Giralda in Seville and the Hassan Tower in Rabat. Last-minute souvenir shopping or a final mint tea at a traditional café.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time: optional visit to the Mellah (Jewish Quarter) and the Lazama Synagogue — a fascinating and often-overlooked layer of Marrakech's multicultural history. Check out of Hotel Aday and arrange private luxury transfer to Marrakech Menara Airport. Allow at least 2.5 hours before departure for check-in and security.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Marrakech Menara Airport. Carry the memories of the Sahara, the souks, and the warmth of Moroccan hospitality.

meals.breakfast: Final riad breakfast — a leisurely spread of all your Moroccan favorites: msemen, beghrir, amlou, fresh orange juice, and mint tea
meals.lunch: Lunch at Café des Épices (75 Rahba Lakdima, Place des Épices) — a beloved Medina institution with rooftop terrace views over the spice square; try the zaalouk, briouats, and fresh lemonade
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight dining

day_by_day.notes: Confirm checkout time with Hotel Aday — standard checkout is typically 12:00 but late checkout may be arranged for a premium. Keep a small amount of Moroccan dirhams for tips and last-minute purchases. Marrakech airport can be busy — arrive early. Declare any argan oil or food products at customs if returning to the EU or US.

query: Morocco Marrakech and Sahara, $1000 solo, 7 days, March
